ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A uniformly distributed random variable \(X\) has probability density function \[ f_x(x)=\frac{1}{10}(u(x+5)-u(x-5)) \] where \(u(\cdot)\) is the unit step function. After passing through the transformation shown in the image, what is the probability density function \(f_Y(y)\) of the transformed random variable \(Y\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The transformation curve in the attached figure is a rectangular pulse: between x=-2.5 and x=2.5, the output y remains 1; outside this interval, the corresponding output is 0. Reasoning: From f_X(x)=1/10(u(x+5)-u(x-5)), it can be known that X is uniformly distributed on [-5,5], with density 1/10. Because the transformation given by the image makes Y=1 when -2.5<=X<=2.5, P(Y=1)=P(-2.5<=X<=2.5)=5*(1/10)=0.5. The total length of the remaining intervals [-5,-2.5) and (2.5,5] is also 5, so P(Y=0)=5*(1/10)=0.5. Thus Y is a discrete random variable that only takes 0 and 1, and its generalized probability density is composed of two Dirac impulses.

method.method_draft: From the text, identify X as uniform on [-5,5] with density 1/10. From the image, identify the transformation as Y=1 when X lies in [-2.5,2.5] and Y=0 otherwise. Compute P(Y=1)=P(-2.5<=X<=2.5)=5/10=0.5 and P(Y=0)=P(X in [-5,-2.5) union (2.5,5])=5/10=0.5. Therefore express the pdf of Y as two atoms: f_Y(y)=0.5 delta(y)+0.5 delta(y-1).
